styleBible:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: final environment production storyboard for a playable 3D platform game. One landscape 16:9 frame at the highest available native resolution, ideally 3840x2160.
Primary request: Redraw image 1 in the premium stylized 3D environment art direction of Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time, especially the pirate level Booty Calls.
Input roles: Image 1 is the CURRENT GAME CAMERA AND LAYOUT reference. Preserve its camera, perspective, route footprint, platform heights, jump gaps, passage openings and principal landmarks. Image 2 is the APPROVED STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its sculpted forms, authored materials, rendering quality and palette, never copy its scene or composition.
Style bible: appealing exaggerated proportions, thick bevelled and subtly bowed timber, curved tapering silhouettes, broad hand-painted wood grain, large sculpted rock planes and deep deliberate creases, restrained edge accents, vivid teal water, warm honey orange timber, brass and coral red cloth, cool blue-purple rock shadows. This is polished stylized 3D game art with coherent physical lighting, not a photoreal painting. Purposeful prop clusters, broad quiet surfaces, clear next landing, strong foreground/middle/background separation. Atmospheric depth, practical lantern pools, legible warm/cool lighting; preserve material midtones in shadow. Avoid repeated tile grain, gritty micro-noise, crude low-poly triangulation and glossy plastic.
Constraints: Keep the playable route and this exact camera recognisable. Improve environmental construction, materials, silhouette and lighting comprehensively. Remove HUD, logos, text, player avatar, floating collectible symbols, timer and checkpoint graphics; reconstruct the environment behind them. No people, other characters, collage, labels, watermark or border. Don't add obstacles across the route.
compositionSource: Current native 3840x2160 player-camera captures at Max quality
review: Original-resolution input and output inspection; no upscaling

supersededDuringReview.scene: Scene: The escape bridge viewed from the broken galleon's bow, facing the treasure cave. Preserve image 1's close player camera and route geometry: narrow wooden bridge runs up the middle into the distance with ONE clearly visible missing span across its full width; the supported far landing turns left toward a broad raised stone treasure floor and a glimpse of the crowned-skull stone portal at upper left. Rock shoulders frame both sides, the broad right wall is close, deep turquoise moonpool below. Rebuild the bridge from thick curved weathered planks on sagging heavy ropes, the rope rails stay OUTSIDE the walkable width and are securely lashed around large stout posts at both banks; crossbearers and robust vertical piles support the far landing. The break must remain a readable jump, do not fill it. Broad sculpted grey-violet limestone lobes with deliberate recesses and curved overhangs, sparse rounded stalactites, no repetitive cave modules or gritty tiled texture. Cool blue cave bounce and a pale roof shaft define the near edge; warm lanterns lead toward the far landing and treasure threshold. Golden treasure glints and pale daylight beyond the skull portal at the back-left reward progress. Match image 2's timber, sculpted rock, water and visual quality only; do NOT put a ship broadside, masts or harbour into this forward-facing view. Clear structurally anchored traversal, charming pirate adventure with real depth.

supersededDuringReview.scene: Scene: The king's ransom, final royal treasure vault. Image 2 is the preceding escape bridge in the same world: use its sculpted rock, gold light, portal and treasure visual language only, NOT its bridge composition. prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: final environment art storyboard for a playable 3D platform game, landscape 16:9, highest available native resolution, ideally 3840x2160.
Primary request: Redraw the supplied game screenshot in the vivid, beautifully sculpted stylized 3D environment art direction of Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time, specifically the pirate level Booty Calls. This should look like a polished screenshot from that caliber of game, not a realistic painting and not a low-quality mesh render.
Input image 1 is the CURRENT LEVEL COMPOSITION REFERENCE. Preserve its player camera, horizon, perspective, the winding boardwalk footprint, elevation and visible gaps, warehouses along the left, open water on the right, and fort-crowned headland straight ahead. It is not a texture or quality reference.
Scene: The customs quay of a Caribbean pirate port at golden hour. A broad timber boardwalk curves from bottom center toward a timber sea-gate under the distant fort. Ochre plaster warehouses with teal shutters, curved terracotta roofs and red cloth awnings hug the left quay. Oversized palms, heavy mooring posts, asymmetrically grouped oak cargo and hanging brass lanterns frame the route. Small anchored sailboats on the right. Build the headland as a few beautifully sculpted large rock masses with broad clean planes, deep creases, rounded bevels and lush foliage ledges, crowned by an exaggerated charming stone fort. The next landing and sea-gate must read clearly.
Art direction: unmistakably premium Crash 4 pirate environment: appealing exaggerated proportions, curved tapering forms, thick rounded timber edges, subtly bowed planks with individually authored broad grain, warm orange ochre and coral reds, turquoise water with graphic foam, saturated but controlled tropical greenery, cool blue-purple shadow planes, coherent stylized PBR shading and painterly albedo. Strong foreground/middle/background separation, quiet surfaces around the route, purposeful compact prop clusters. Soft golden rim light, cool ambient bounce, restrained depth haze, no muddy shadows.
Constraints: retain composition and traversable route from the screenshot. Improve art quality and physical construction thoroughly. Remove all HUD, lettering, timer, logo, floating collectibles, player avatar and checkpoint graphics; render the underlying walkable deck cleanly. No other characters. No generic photoreal rock noise, repeating tiled stone or wood grain, thin ruler-straight modular edges, scattered confetti props, poster composition, collage, border, watermark or text. One complete landscape environment frame.
prompts.title: The customs quay

prompts.scene: Scene: The broken cargo jetty. Preserve the foreground timber platform, its visible broken jump gaps and the alternating dock spans leading straight toward the great sea-cave in the fort headland. Keep the giant timber hoist to the left of the route, quay edge along far left, anchored sailing lighter to the right, open water below. Rebuild dock piles as chunky barnacled oak rooted in the seabed, with diagonal braces and stout rope lashings. Use slightly bowed broad planks, a clear broken edge silhouette at each jump, compact cargo stacks at outer edges, a single suspended loading pallet offset from the route. Red cloth accents and amber lanterns. Match the approved fort, tropical vegetation, honey/golden-hour light and bright turquoise sea. The headland has large quiet sculpted grey-blue rock faces and lush leafy ledges, with the warm inviting tunnel mouth central. No warehouses inserted into this closer view.
